name: BERTRAM
taetigkeit: Bookseller’s apprentice (1837), becoming head clerk/manager by the age of 21

name: BERTRAM
taetigkeit: contributor to various periodicals, including Chambers’s Journaland Hogg's Instructor

name: BERTRAM
taetigkeit: editor, and later proprietor, of the North Briton (1855-73)

name: BERTRAM
taetigkeit: proprietor of the short-run Bawbee (1856) and the slightly more successful Scottish Thistle (to 1859)

name: BERTRAM
taetigkeit: assistant editor of the Glasgow News (1873-4)

name: BERTRAM
taetigkeit: journalist and author, contributing to the provincial weekly press and miscellaneous periodicals (1874-92)

name: BINNS
taetigkeit: assistant to brother in plumbing business (1794-8)

name: BINNS
taetigkeit: proprietor of the Republican Argus when living in Pennsylvania (1801-7)

name: BINNS
taetigkeit: editor of the Democratic Press, when in Philadelphia (1807-)

name: BLATCHFORD
taetigkeit: First employment was as odd-job boy in lithographic printing works

name: BLATCHFORD
taetigkeit: enlisted in army, achieving rank of sergeant (1871-7)

name: BLATCHFORD
taetigkeit: began writing career in 1882 when article published in The Yorkshireman, subsequently working as a weekly columnist and news reporter

name: BLATCHFORD
taetigkeit: resigned from Manchester Sunday Chronicle (1891), to start, with 4 others, the Clarion

name: BRIERLEY
taetigkeit: At age 5 had to assist in bread-winning by door-to-door hawking

name: BRIERLEY
taetigkeit: was later ‘put to the bobbin wheel’ at home, followed by a brief spell in a factory as a piecer, eventually becoming a domestic hand-loom weaver. During period of trade depression he found employment dragging coals from the coal pits. Moved to Manchester to work in various silk manufacturers’ warehouses (up to 1860s)

name: BRIERLEY
taetigkeit: adopted literature as his profession, contributing articles, poems and short stories to a variety of newspapers and journals

name: BRIERLEY
taetigkeit: editor of own journal, Country Words (1869-75), which was successful until death of daughter caused him to lose interest. Visited America and then returned to literary profession running his own Ben Brierley’s Journal (1869-91)

name: BRITTON
taetigkeit: Assisted mother in making bread and working on the farm (1784-7)

name: BRITTON
taetigkeit: recited and sang in a theatre (1799)

name: BRITTON
taetigkeit: adopted writing as a profession, c.1799/1800, with his first book being published in 1799. Also served as surveyor and clerk to the local Board of Commissioners. Was granted a civil list pension of $75 in 1852

name: BROOKS
taetigkeit: Started work at local mill as a half-timer at age 10 as an errand-boy, then as a reacher-in and as a cut-looker’s assistant (to age 13)

name: BURGESS
taetigkeit: Started work in a card-cutting room at age 6, remaining full-time for 2 years

name: BURGESS
taetigkeit: half-time ‘little piecer’ from age 8-13, then full-time as a ‘big piecer’

name: BURGESS
taetigkeit: worked as a cotton operative until aged 28, but with short spells in a print works and a cardsheet manufactory

name: BURGESS
taetigkeit: started own (short-lived) paper, the Oldham Operative (1884)

name: BURGESS
taetigkeit: sub-editor of the Cotton Factory Times (1885-9)

name: BURGESS
taetigkeit: continued to work as a journalist, poet and writer

name: BURGESS
taetigkeit: organising secretary for Independent Labour Party (1897-1902)

name: BURGESS
taetigkeit: on editorial staff of the London Evening Standard (1919) and Pall Mall Gazette
boot-cleaner and tap-polisher in an hotel
employed in an advertising agency and as a theatre utility man
spent 7 years in the office of a literary agency
received commissions which enabled him to devote himself to literary work

name: CAMPBELL
taetigkeit: editor of Bradford Observer (from 1860) and for over 26 years of the Northern Chronicle, Inverness

name: CATLING
taetigkeit: Forced to start work at age 11 owing to decline in father’s business, commencing in the offices of the Cambridge Chronicle

name: CATLING
taetigkeit: apprentice compositor (5 years) on Lloyd’s Weekly Newspaper, remaining with the same paper all his working life, rising from compositor to sub-editor and, eventually, editor. Retired, 1907

name: CATTON
taetigkeit: employed in chemical works (to 1820), but forced to leave through ill-health

name: CATTON
taetigkeit: took a general shop at Plaistow (1820-56)

name: EVETT
taetigkeit: First employment was in a rope and twine factory

name: EVETT
taetigkeit: apprenticed to printing firm in Colchester for 6 years (c.1900-6)

name: EVETT
taetigkeit: journeyman compositor (1906-). Engaged in odd-jobs after the war before becoming an assistant reader, and eventually a reader for the Law Times, and then for the Financial Times (1928-40)

name: GALLACHER
taetigkeit: Worked as a milkboy in the hours before school (1891-3)

name: GALLACHER
taetigkeit: employed in a sanitary engineering shop (1895) and in various other factories (1895-1909)

name: GALLACHER
taetigkeit: employed in the Albion Motor Works (1910-12/13

name: GALLACHER
taetigkeit: 1914-). Was on the staff Daily Worker for a short period. Elected as the first Communist MP (1935-50), representing West Fife

name: GARRATT
taetigkeit: Factory worker at a gas meter manufactory (1906-14)

name: GARRATT
taetigkeit: journalist, on the staff of John Bull and the English Review

name: HOGG
taetigkeit: tenant farmer, while continuing his distinguished literary pursuits

name: KITZ
taetigkeit: Supported self from very early age by taking jobs as an errand-boy, porter and messenger

name: KITZ
taetigkeit: was articled to a garment-dyer but soon left this employment to go ‘on the tramp’

name: MOFFAT
taetigkeit: worked for short periods as a printer’s devil and shop-boy

name: MOFFAT
taetigkeit: enlisted in British Navy by deception when under age (1857) and was soon discharged

name: MOFFAT
taetigkeit: apprentice sailor on a collier brig

name: MOFFAT
taetigkeit: subsequently worked as a ship’s pilot, cook and steward before becoming a ship’s captain. Gave up his command in 1891, and employed as superintendent of the working of steamers in the London docks (1891-1905)

name: MORRISON
taetigkeit: circulation manager of the first official Labour paper, the Daily Citizen (1912-15)

name: MORRISON
taetigkeit: part-time secretary of London Labour Party (1915-47)

name: MORRISON
taetigkeit: after 1915, politics, as either organiser or MP, was his sole occupation. MP for Hackney South (1923-4

name: OKEY
taetigkeit: master basket-maker (1882-96), combined with literary work and foreign travel

name: OKEY
taetigkeit: assistant examiner in Italian to the Civil Service Commission (1918)

name: OKEY
taetigkeit: professor of Italian, Cambridge University (1919-28). Accepted commission in 1903 to write “The Story of Venice’ (published as writing and publication of similar works

name: REAKES
taetigkeit: teacher for the International Correspondence Schools (1911-16)

name: REDFERN
taetigkeit: remained a shop assistant until 1898 when he became a storekeeper for the Manchester Vegetarian Society

name: REDFERN
taetigkeit: desk clerk at Manchester Co-operative Wholesale Society, becoming sub-editor and then managing editor of that society’s publications, and its historian (to 1938)

name: SEXTON
taetigkeit: First employment was punching holes in clog irons (for 1 week), followed by a job at the local glass works. Stowed away on a sailing ship (1868) and became a sailor

name: SEXTON
taetigkeit: laboured at a chemical factory (for 3 years)

name: SEXTON
taetigkeit: casual dock labourer, but was marked out as an agitator and found it difficult to find employment. Worked for a short time as a steamship painter before beginning own business, running a coalyard, with donkey and cart. MP for St. Helens (1918-31)

name: WARDLE
taetigkeit: parliamentary secretary to Board of Trade, and later, Ministry of Labour (from 1917). Elected Labour MP for Stockport in 1906. Resigned his office and parliamentary seat in 1920 owing to ill-health

name: WATSON
taetigkeit: apprentice builder (1882), remaining in the same trade for the rest of his working life

name: WATSON
taetigkeit: clerk of works, supervising the erection of a spinning mill (1905)

name: WATSON
taetigkeit: appointed first manager of Manchester Corporation Direct Works Department (1920-3), and then held the same post in Barnsley

name: WELCH
taetigkeit: Employed in a tea broker’s establishment (1894)

name: WELCH
taetigkeit: appointed secretary of the Bible Training College (1904)

name: WELCH
taetigkeit: editor of the Berean Expositor for more than 50 years

name: WELCH
taetigkeit: Principal of the Chapel of the Opened Book, Finsbury Square, London

name: WILSON
taetigkeit: Began work ‘when very young milking cows’‚ then farm-boy during day and in a card shop, carding teeth, by night. Later worked as a bobbin-winder (c.1838)

name: WILSON
taetigkeit: and, finally, as an expert horticulturalist

name: AIRD
taetigkeit: apprentice compositor, becoming a journeyman in 1839

name: AIRD
taetigkeit: foreman of print shop (for 7 years), then a manager

name: CHURCH
taetigkeit: lecturer for the British Council throughout Europe, India and Africa

name: HETHERINGTON
taetigkeit: Apprenticed to parliamentary printer, Luke Hansard (1805), and eventually became a compositor. Published pamphlets on his own account as well as for others (1822-)

name: WATSON
taetigkeit: At age 12 was bound to clergyman as general servant, but indentures cancelled after 6 years owing to death of master’s wife

name: WATSON
taetigkeit: shopman to Mr. Carlile, and later manager of his business (1822-6), though interrupted by periods of imprisonment for selling liberal and freethinking literature
